newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy drafts milk sector bill as farmers protest.
newsitem.headline: Italy drafts milk sector bill as farmers protest.

text.p: Italy's cabinet on Friday approved a draft law to provide compensation for dairy farmers who have had their milk output cut under tough EU quotas, but farmers staging a second day of protests said the plans did not go far enough.
A statement said the bill included "provisions for direct measures to improve the position of producers who have suffered reductions of individual quotas". It gave no details.
The plans fell short of farmers' demands to have the state help bear the burden of EU "super levy" fines for overproduction and sparked fresh confrontations with police in northern Italy.

In Milan, where some 1,500 producers with 700 tractors have paralysed traffic and virtually cut off the main Linate airport, extra detachments of the paramilitary Carabinieri police were on the streets.
One producer lay down to try to prevent the police manoeuvres and was almost run over.
"It (the bill) is a provocation," said Aldo Bettinelli, one of the producers involved in the Milan demonstrations.

"We'll keep this up until we get a reply from Rome," said another. "Half of the milk that arrives on Italians' tables is imported. If we add to that the fines, it's clear that things can't go on like this."

Media reports say Italian farmers face 420 billion lire ($270 million) in European Union "super levy" fines for overproduction. Estimates from member states place Italy as the worst offender for exceeding its national quota.
Late last year, an EU Commission official said milk production in the 15-member bloc was 1.1 million tonnes over quota, with Italy accounting for 470,000 tonnes, or nearly half.
An agriculture ministry spokeswoman said Italy had overproduced by 400,000 tonnes.
The fines hit individual farmers and not the state. Farmers want the government to ensure that they do not have to shoulder the full burden themselves.
Farmers from other milk producing regions in northern Italy have also staged protests and some 200 of them arrived in Milan from Parma to join the demonstration.

The government statement said the draft bill would make regional authorities responsible for enforcing milk production limits and said the measures would "bring the quota system more in line with farmers' and regional requirements".
